answer: A submission bridge counts each job thread: one identity may send at most three per epoch. Each identity locks a 90-credit bond; a fourth thread burns it and voids the earlier three. Each thread bears a pigment stamp bound to its key and counter slot, so a copied thread fails the check. For 3,000 jobs a farm needs 1,000 identities, 90,000 credits, and 3,000 separate jobs, since threads cannot merge and the kth fake still pays 90. A counter-reset ring fails, as the counter follows the funding key. An honest agent locks one bond and keeps it. Anyone can recheck the counter, stamps, and ledger.
